extracted.intended_audience: inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF) administrators, billing/compliance officers, clinicians responsible for IRF-PAI data, and Medicare policy/stakeholder staff
extracted.subtask_short: IRF PPS compliance and QRP reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and methodological standards for updating IRF prospective payment system (PPS) rates for FY2025 and for changes to the Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility Quality Reporting Program (IRF QRP) (including IRF-PAI standardized items) beginning FY2028. Includes payment calculation methods, data submission rules, and associated adjustments and penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update CMG relative weights and ALOS values for FY 2025
rubrics_metrics.description: Update the CMG relative weights and average length of stay values for FY 2025, using updated FY 2023 IRF claims and FY 2022 IRF cost report data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS uses the most recent available data to update CMG relative weights and ALOS values; changes are implemented in a budget-neutral manner and affect distribution of payments across CMGs and tiers. Table 2 in the rule lists CMG/tier relative weights and ALOS for FY2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology to calculate CMG relative weights
rubrics_metrics.description: The process to calculate the CMG relative weights follows these steps: Step 1. Estimate the effects that comorbidities have on costs. Step 2. Adjust the cost of each Medicare discharge (case) to reflect the effects found in Step 1. Step 3. Use the adjusted costs from Step 2 to calculate CMG relative weights, using the hospital-specific relative value method. Step 4. Normalize the FY 2025 CMG relative weights using a normalization factor that results in the average CMG relative weights in FY 2025 being the same as the average CMG relative weights in the FY 2024 IRF PPS final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses detailed CCR data from cost reports of IRF provider units of primary acute care hospitals; the Grouper/IRF-PAI data feed into classification. Normalization preserves average weight parity with FY2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget-neutral implementation of CMG revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: CMG relative weight revisions are implemented such that total estimated aggregate payments to IRFs for FY 2025 are the same with or without the changes (i.e., in a budget-neutral manner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS calculates a budget neutrality factor by: (1) estimating total IRF PPS payments for FY2025 with no CMG changes; (2) estimating total payments applying CMG changes; (3) dividing amount (1) by amount (2) to get the factor (0.9976 for FY2025); (4) applying factor to the FY2025 standard payment amount after wage adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of hospital-specific relative value (HSRV) method
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS uses a hospital-specific relative value method to estimate operating and capital costs of IRFs when calculating CMG relative weights and does not adopt average-cost weighting for FY2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS explains HSRV places emphasis on more efficient IRF providers; commenters suggested average-cost weighting, but CMS declined pending careful evaluation due to major distributional impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data recency principle for payment calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the most current and complete data available (for FY2025 CMS used FY2023 claims and FY2022 cost report data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more recent data become available between proposed and final rule publication, CMS may use such data to determine CMG weights and ALOS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of case-level and facility-level adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply adjustments for interrupted stays, transfers, short stays, deaths, geographic wage index, percentage of low-income patients (LIP), rural location, teaching status, and outlier payments to the IRF unadjusted prospective payment rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These adjustments are applied via the MAC Pricer using CMG number and other claim/provider-specific data; FY2006 and later rulemaking established many of these adjustments (e.g., teaching status effective FY2006).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation and update of IRF standard payment conversion factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe and calculate the IRF standard payment conversion factor for FY2025 using the methods described in the FY2024 IRF PPS final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard payment conversion factor is computed as part of payment-rate setting and is adjusted by budget-neutral wage adjustment factor and other statutory updates described in section V of the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update IRF PPS payment rates by market basket and productivity adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Update the FY2025 IRF PPS payment rates by the market basket increase factor with a productivity adjustment required by section 1886(j)(3)(C)(ii)(I) of the Social Security Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule applies the statutory productivity adjustment when computing the market-basket-based update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update wage index using revised OMB market area delineations and phase-out of rural adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt revised OMB core-based statistical area delineations (OMB Bulletin No. 23-01) for the IRF PPS wage index and apply a 3-year phase-out of the rural adjustment for IRFs changing from rural to urban.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wage index changes affect geographic adjustments to payments; the rule describes adoption of OMB changes and transitional phase-out timing for affected IRFs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update outlier threshold and CCR ceilings/averages
rubrics_metrics.description: Update the outlier threshold amount for FY2025 and update the cost-to-charge ratio (CCR) ceiling and urban/rural average CCRs for FY2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These updates affect calculation of outlier payments and the cost estimation methodology used in deriving relative weights and payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRF-PAI completion and Grouper classification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon admission and discharge of Medicare Part A and Medicare Advantage patients, IRFs must complete the appropriate sections of the IRF-PAI and electronically encode all required data into IRF-PAI software (Grouper software classifies patients into CMGs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grouper produces a five-character CMG number (first char = comorbidity tier alpha, last four numeric). Grouper is available for free from CMS and embedded in iQIES. IRF-PAI data feed to claims/Grouper for payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission of Medicare claims per ASCA/HIPAA
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be submitted as HIPAA-compliant electronic claims, except where ASCA permits paper claims or the Secretary waives electronic form requirements in specific circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 3 of ASCA requires electronic claims submission and authorizes waivers where electronic submission isn't available or for small providers; instructions for paper claims are available in CMS manuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-stay transfer/per diem adjustment determined by ALOS
rubrics_metrics.description: The ALOS for each CMG is used to determine when an IRF discharge meets the definition of a short stay transfer, which results in a per diem case level adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated ALOS values for FY2025 are provided; these values are operational inputs to detect short stay transfers and compute per-diem adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption/modification/removal of IRF-PAI standardized patient assessment data elements (IRF QRP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalize collection of four new items as standardized patient assessment data elements (one Living Situation item, two Food items, one Utilities item) and modify one item (Transportation) in the IRF-PAI beginning with the FY2028 IRF QRP; finalize removal of Item 14. Admission Class from the IRF-PAI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These standardized items must be collected and submitted using IRF-PAI beginning FY2028; CMS also summarized comments on future QRP measure concepts and a possible IRF star rating system.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRF QRP compliance penalty (reporting-based reduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 1886(j)(7)(A)(i) of the Act, beginning in FY2014 CMS applies a 2-percentage point reduction to the market basket increase factor for an IRF for a FY if the IRF does not comply with the requirements of the IRF QRP for that FY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting-based reductions are not cumulative and apply only for the fiscal year involved; noncompliance can thus reduce the update applied to payments for that year.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRF-PAI submission for all patients regardless of payer
rubrics_metrics.description: As revised in the FY2023 IRF PPS final rule, all IRFs must submit IRF-PAI data on each patient receiving care in an IRF, regardless of payer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expands IRF-PAI data collection beyond Medicare patients and supports QRP and other reporting/quality measurement efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Grouper/iQIES tools and software availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Grouper software is available for free download on the CMS website and is embedded in the internet Quality Improvement and Evaluation System (iQIES) user tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IRFs should use the official Grouper implementation to generate CMG numbers and to ensure consistent classification for payment and reporting; links are provided in the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of COVID-19 PHE flexibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies adopted as flexibilities during the COVID-19 PHE (e.g., 3-hour rule waiver and post-admission physician evaluation removal during PHE) were implemented via interim final rules and some flexibilities were terminated upon HHS declaration of PHE expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PHE expiration resulted in termination of certain waivers (e.g., 3-hour rule waiver at §412.622(a)(3)(ii)); CMS notes which flexibilities were permanent (post-admission physician evaluation documentation requirement removed permanently beginning FY2021).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment summary and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS summarizes public comments received on proposals and provides responses, and may consider comments for future refinements or refer them to subject matter experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS received comments from trade associations, IRFs, clinicians, and others; it addresses out-of-scope comments by acknowledging and possibly forwarding them to appropriate experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and analysis of distributional effects
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS reports distributional effects of CMG relative weight changes (e.g., percentage of cases with changes in weight ranges) to show how revisions affect case distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 3 presents counts/percentages of cases with increases/decreases by magnitude (e.g., 99.2% of cases change by less than 5%); distributional analysis demonstrates anticipated payment shifting across CMGs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to use IRF provider-unit CCR data in cost calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed cost-to-charge ratio (CCR) data from cost reports of IRF provider units of primary acute care hospitals (not CCRs from associated primary care hospitals) are used to calculate IRFs' average costs per case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach was adopted in the FY2009 IRF PPS final rule and is used to ensure the CCRs reflect IRF provider unit costs, informing relative weights and payment calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of health equity and SDOH measures in QRP development
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS discusses health equity reporting (Health Equity Confidential Feedback Reports stratified by dual-enrollment status and race/ethnicity) and consideration of health-related social needs items (e.g., transportation, food, utilities) in QRP measure concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS released Health Equity Confidential Feedback Reports (DTC and MSPB) and references available education/outreach materials and research supporting inclusion of SDOH items; IRFs can access training materials and cue cards on the IRF QRP Training web page.
